tagline: Sync GitHub issues and PRs to Airtable so your project database always reflects your code reality
metaTitle: GitHub + Airtable Integration: Issues to an Airtable Roadmap
metaDescription: Sync GitHub issues to an Airtable roadmap base, track PR cycle time and update release tracking on each release. GAIA builds the reporting. See the setup steps.
intro:
Airtable's flexible database structure makes it the go-to tool for custom project tracking, roadmapping, and engineering metrics—but keeping a base in sync with GitHub is a manual, time-consuming process. Issues get logged but never make it to the roadmap base. PRs are merged but the corresponding record stays stuck in In Progress. Leadership dashboards built on the base are always a few days behind reality.

GAIA propagates changes through triggers so your custom project databases stay accurate without manual imports. Issues created in GitHub appear in your roadmap base automatically. PR status changes update the corresponding record. Releases trigger new rows in your release tracking base with the relevant metadata.

For product-engineering teams that have built custom workflows for planning and reporting, this integration removes the manual data entry burden that makes those workflows unsustainable at scale.

useCases.title: Sync GitHub issues to an Airtable roadmap base
useCases.description: When an issue is created or updated, GAIA creates or updates the corresponding record in your roadmap base, mapping issue fields like labels, assignees, and milestones to your custom columns.

useCases.title: Track PR cycle time in Airtable
useCases.description: GAIA records PR open and merge timestamps in a base, enabling you to build custom views and formulas that track engineering cycle time, review duration, and throughput metrics without manual data collection.

useCases.title: Update release tracking base on GitHub releases
useCases.description: When a release is published, GAIA adds a new record to your release tracking base with the version number, date, number of issues closed, and a link to the release notes.

useCases.title: Weekly engineering metrics compiled into a summary record
useCases.description: GAIA compiles weekly engineering metrics (issues opened and closed, PRs merged, releases shipped) into a summary record that feeds your leadership reporting views automatically.

useCases.title: Map labels to select fields
useCases.description: Issue labels like priority::high or type::bug are automatically mapped to corresponding single-select or multi-select fields, ensuring your database categorization stays consistent with the labels in the repository.

howItWorks.step: Connect GitHub and Airtable to GAIA
howItWorks.description: Authorize your repositories and workspace in GAIA's settings. Specify which base and table to sync with each repository.

howItWorks.step: Map repository fields to table columns
howItWorks.description: Configure how repository data maps to your table schema: which fields populate which columns, how to handle new labels, and whether to create new records or update existing ones.
GAIA monitors the repositories for issue, PR, and release events and updates the base as changes are detected. Your dashboards and views always reflect current repository data without manual imports.

faqs.question: Can GAIA sync data from Airtable back to GitHub?
faqs.answer: Yes. Sync works in both directions through configured triggers—if you update an issue status in the base, GAIA can update the corresponding issue label or assignee. This is useful for product managers who manage priority in the base but want changes reflected in the repository.

faqs.question: Does GAIA work with the linked records feature?
faqs.answer: Yes. GAIA can create linked records—for example, linking a PR record to the issue records it closes—preserving the relational structure of your data rather than flattening everything into a single table.

faqs.question: Can I use native automations alongside GAIA's sync?
faqs.answer: Yes. GAIA's record updates trigger native automations just like manual edits do, so you can combine the sync with the base's own automation features for additional downstream actions.

faqs.question: How does GAIA handle deleted issues?
faqs.answer: When an issue is deleted, GAIA can either delete the corresponding record, mark it as deleted in a status field, or leave it as an archived record—depending on your configuration preference.
